items.headline: Chip stocks crash 5.9% and OpenAI delays its IPO after Amodei's 'We Must Pace the Frontier' triggers CEO consensus on slowing AI, hours before the Fed's rate call
items.note: Philadelphia Semiconductor Index -5.9% (Nvidia -3.4%, Micron -7%), 10-year yield breached 5% for first time since 2007, Altman called an IPO 'ill-advised' right now citing Amodei's essay, Fed decision due 2026-09-16. No queue title fits directly, but it sits at the intersection of leadership trade-offs (a CEO publicly choosing restraint) and capital allocation (markets repricing AI-company valuations in real time) — strong candidate for a fresh working title rather than a forced fit.

items.headline: OpenAI's Videos API and all Sora 2 models are removed on 24 September with no successor named
items.note: Confirmed on OpenAI's own deprecations page: notice given 2026-03-24, removal 2026-09-24, replacement column reads '---' for every Sora 2 entry — a vendor pulling a capability outright rather than migrating customers to a successor. Notice period was six months, not ninety days, so the queue title's literal figure doesn't match even though the theme does; worth checking before reusing the number in copy.

items.headline: Anthropic still targeting a $2 trillion October IPO on Morgan Stanley/Goldman/JPMorgan underwriting, even as OpenAI just called its own listing 'ill-advised'
items.note: Target $2tn valuation vs the $965bn May Series H-1 mark; three-pillar pricing/access/privacy strategy ahead of listing. This is a live continuation of an already-published essay — the fresh hook is the divergence: Anthropic pressing ahead the same week Altman pauses OpenAI's own IPO plans on safety grounds.

items.headline: Google cuts AI Plus 37%, OpenAI reportedly weighing 'drastic' token price cuts to counter Anthropic — the price war is intensifying this week
items.note: Google's AI Plus subscription cut from $7.99 to $4.99/month announced this week; WSJ reports OpenAI weighing further token cuts, no figures confirmed yet. Anthropic's own Yahoo Finance piece (item above) separately confirms a 75% cut to cache-read pricing ($1.00 to $0.25/M tokens) — corroborating detail worth folding in if this one gets picked up.

items.headline: Oracle to raise $45–50bn in debt and equity for AI data centres after Q2 free cash flow ran negative $13bn on $12bn of capex
items.note: Half debt (investment-grade bond), half equity (mandatory convertible preferred plus a new $20bn ATM programme); investor concern centres on OpenAI's creditworthiness as the anchor customer behind the 359% RPO surge. Reads as the inverse of the Buffett fortress-balance-sheet family — a hyperscaler levering up rather than hoarding cash — but doesn't clear the bar for a proposed title on magnitude alone; flagging as background for whoever picks up the depreciation-cliff piece once hyperscaler earnings land in late October.
